subject: Performance SLO: Context window token limits and latency impact - post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex King <alex.king@finco.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finco.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Performance SLO: Context window token limits and latency impact — post-call recap

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side on the performance / SLO topics you raised:

Summary of requirements we captured
- Typical request: ~800–1,200 input tokens, ~200–400 output tokens.
- Heavy tail: occasional documents that require ~20k tokens of context (indexing + retrieval chunks).
- Latency targets: p95 <= 800ms for typical short prompts; for long-context workflows we expect streaming output with p95 time-to-first-byte <= 1s and completion times up to ~2–3s depending on sequence length.
- Concurrency: steady-state 40–60 concurrent requests, spiking to ~100 for batch runs.
- Throughput: roughly 500k–1M tokens/day.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + custom retention controls (you mentioned audit-log export).

Key constraints we discussed
- Context window (input + output) will materially affect per-request latency and token compute cost. Larger context increases attention cost O(n^2) for some kernels; we mitigate with chunked retrieval, KV-cache reuse, and model/kernel selection.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency for long outputs but doesn’t reduce total compute for full generations.

What Redwood proposes
- For typical short prompts: Redwood Dedicated capacity + tuned batching gives p95 < 800ms for 1k token requests.
- For long-context workflows: recommend retrieval chunking + progressive streaming; use a model variant with large context optimized kernels (we have verified performance profiles for 32k/64k contexts).
- Pilot: 7-day PoC on Dedicated with a baseline config (2 reserved GPUs, autoscale policy, streaming enabled) so we can produce real latency/throughput numbers on your traffic.

Attachments: SLO-summary.pdf (high-level SLO tradeoffs), latency-metrics.csv (sample benchmarks).

Next steps / mutual action plan
1) You share a 48-hour sample of representative traffic (headers stripped) — we can use this to size the pilot (Alex, you mentioned you could provide this).
2) Redwood stands up a 7-day Dedicated pilot and runs the traffic; we will instrument p50/p95/p99 for time-to-first-byte and time-to-complete, and token-cost estimates.
3) Technical sync (30–45 min) to confirm chunking strategy and streaming hooks — propose Tue or Wed next week.

If that sounds right I’ll schedule the pilot kickoff and loop in our solutions engineer.

Thanks,

--

Subject: Re: Performance SLO: Context window token limits and latency impact — post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Typical input is closer to 1k tokens, agreed. The heavy-tail comes from our ingestion pipeline where a single customer session may generate ~15–25k tokens after concatenating retrieval chunks. We need the option to pass that full context occasionally (not every request).
- Latency: we’re comfortable with streaming for the long requests. For short prompts we’re aiming for p95 <= 800ms (as you captured). For streaming, time-to-first-byte is the main metric — <= 1s ideal.
- Concurrency: 40 steady, spikes to 100 for scheduled batches at EOD.

A couple of questions:
1) How does Redwood handle tokenization differences / token counting across models (we need to ensure consistent billing and SLOs)?
2) For the pilot, will you support chunking on the Redwood side or do we need to implement client-side chunking?
3) Any default safeguards if someone sends a >64k token request? Rate-limit or reject?

I attached a small sample of the tail traffic (sample-traffic.json) — it’s scrubbed. Could you confirm receipt? Also looping Priya here on procurement and SOC2 evidence requests.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO: Context window token limits and latency impact — post-call recap

Alex — got the sample, thanks (attached). Answers inline below.

> How does Redwood handle tokenization differences / token counting across models?
We normalize billing and SLO accounting to token counts after model-specific tokenization. In practice we provide a tokenization preview for your payloads during the pilot so you can see exact token counts per model variant; that preview also feeds into our cost estimates. For SLOs we tie latency expectations to the observed tokenized length distribution for the chosen model.

> For the pilot, will you support chunking on the Redwood side or do we need to implement client-side chunking?
We can support both:
- Client-side chunking: recommended if you want full control over retrieval logic.
- Server-side progressive retrieval & concat: our SDK can optionally perform chunked requests with streaming assembly; this reduces client work but we’ll need to agree on boundary conditions for deduping and overlap. We’ll include a recommended chunker as part of the pilot checklist.

> Default safeguards for >64k token requests?
We enforce configurable per-request token limits at the gateway. Default behavior is to reject requests exceeding the configured maximum with a 413-like error; for Dedicated customers we can raise the limit with service-level guardrails (safety caps, queueing). We’ll surface these in the pilot config.

Performance notes (brief)
- Latency scales roughly superlinearly with sequence length for some kernels; switching to attention optimizations and longer-context kernels reduces that, but compute still increases.
- Batching helps throughput but increases tail latency under high concurrency; we’ll recommend a small, bounded batch window for low-latency paths and a separate high-throughput path for batch jobs.
- Streaming: time-to-first-byte is small (you see partial tokens quickly) but total compute/cost aligns with total tokens generated.

Proposed MAP (updated)
1) We’ll run your 48–72 hour sample through a tokenization preview and sizing script (I’ll share results).
2) Redwood provisions a 7-day Dedicated pilot (streaming enabled + guardrail limits at 64k default).
3) Technical sync next Tue — Steph (cc’d) will own the pilot runbook and instrumentation.

If you confirm the pilot, I’ll share the pilot checklist and DocuSign statement of work for provisioning.

Attachments: pilot-setup-checklist.docx (pilot runbook)

Best,
